S15v13-H2P2: Sénégal passed a law in March 2026 (Law No. 2026-08) that increased the penalty for consensual same-sex intimacy to 5 to 10 years in prison, and it also made public advocacy for homosexuality a crime. Homosexuals were already facing arrests, family rejection, harassment, assault and mob violence, but some say they're actually protected once they're arrested, because then at least the mob can't get at them. I'm not going to praise communal belonging and ignore the people who have to hide who they are to survive it, or leave.
S15v13-H2P2+prev:

S15v13-H3P3: This is also the thorny boundary issue of living without money inside a money-based society. Life inside the commune can go without cash, but you'll still need money for taxes, hospital bills, visas, school fees, family obligations, buying in tools etc. That doesn't mean going back to individual wages inside the commune, but it does mean someone has to handle it! Who's that going to be? And the commune has to work out how much shared cash it keeps for these things, and how to stop access to outside money from creating a new status hierarchy.
S15v13-H3P5: Some Zapatista communities used to try to stop their young people from leaving, which is a version of the same outside-work problem. Now they talk it through with them instead: it's OK to go and work elsewhere, as long as the migrants keep certain defined obligations to the community. That doesn't make the pull between leaving and belonging go away, but at least now it's something they can name and negotiate. I understand the motivation to negotiate like that, but I think it's not a full solution either.

I got a taste of that at a Unitarian youth camp, and it's still one of the freest memories I have. ZEGG's Kinderhaus works from a similar intuition. Adults take care of safety on the outside, but kids still get a world of their own.

This could be badly misunderstood, so the safeguards need to be explicit. The adults still have to pay attention to what goes on in a children's territory. Older kids can't be allowed to boss the younger ones around there. And keeping secrets can't be treated as independence.

I also reject the suburban panic that treats every warm relationship between a child and an unrelated adult as suspicious. It's good for kids to have a whole bunch of grownups who know them and enjoy them, who would notice when something changes, and who would act when something's wrong. When adults panic like that, kids can lose all those grownups without the panic actually preventing abuse.
